items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: That was Celestine, William Racely, John Marrero, Simon Marrero, Paul Barnes

ctx.x: Here's one other thing I heard once, something about you went up in an airplane.

Did, Friday, June of 1924. Gates, Flying Cycles, used to come from California every summer. We were playing at that time at Francina's Restaurant at Spanish Fort. And Mr. George Gates engaged us to play in the airplane. Let me get that. That was Celestine, William Racely, John Marrero, Simon Marrero, Paul Barnes, and Williton, a fellow by the name of Williton, on drum at that time.
Could you get out the whole band in the plane? No. The plane big enough then? Two of us. Two at a time.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: We had two in. Tom Benton was good. John Marrero was good. He was a banjo player and could sing and very good.

ctx.x: Sometimes. Yeah, oh yeah. You'd do that, that action and all that was the funny things that you played. It was pretty good. Well, we got along very good. We had a wonderful, good banjo player. We had two in. Tom Benton was good. John Marrero was good. He was a banjo player and could sing and very good. He had piano piano, I know, routine as we called it. Couldn't read but he could play, he could cut it. Very good. And then the girl was good. She's still playing. She making money at her. Sweet Emma?
Yeah. I got a phone up I've been trying to get all yesterday.
